name: Bikri
title: Father of the rebel Sheba
summary: Bikri was a Benjamite known as the father of Sheba, the man who led a rebellion against King David after Absalom's revolt. Bikri himself plays no direct role in the story, but his name is linked to his son Sheba's uprising, which threatened to split David's kingdom. Sheba is repeatedly referred to as "Sheba son of Bikri" in 2 Samuel.

keyEvents.title: Sheba's rebellion against David
keyEvents.description: Bikri's son Sheba blew the trumpet and urged the tribes of Israel to abandon David, triggering a serious revolt after Absalom's fall.

keyEvents.title: David orders pursuit of Sheba
keyEvents.description: King David recognized that Sheba son of Bikri was a greater threat than Absalom had been, and sent his men to pursue him.

keyEvents.title: Joab pursues Sheba to Abel-Beth-Maacah
keyEvents.description: Joab and his forces pursued Sheba son of Bikri all the way to the city of Abel-Beth-Maacah, where they laid siege to it.

keyEvents.title: A wise woman saves the city
keyEvents.description: A wise woman in Abel-Beth-Maachah negotiated with Joab and persuaded the city's inhabitants to behead Sheba son of Bichri, throwing his head over the wall so that the rebellion ended.
